newsitem.title: USA: GM to speed up dealership changes - WSJ.
newsitem.headline: GM to speed up dealership changes - WSJ.

text.p: General Motors Corp is accelerating its effort to overhaul and consolidate its auto-dealership network, the Wall Street Journal said.

In Friday's electronic edition, the Journal said the company has been quietly pushing up its multibillion-dollar drive to get dealers to relocate to busier neighborhoods, combine with other dealer, change their vehicle offerings or sell out and close up shop.
In 1996, its dealership ranks shrank by 175 to 8,300. GM's marketing executives said they expect to complete changes or take action regarding between 700 and 800 dealerships next year.
Eventually, GM expects to eliminate about 1,000 of its U.S. dealers.
"The challenge we have now is to go faster because the competitive situation is heating up," a GM spokesman told the Journal.
